name: Indigo Denim Wrap Midi Skirt
history: For Gucci’s Spring/Summer 2000 collection, Tom Ford paired pared-back silhouettes with punk references. The exposed pin engraved with the Gucci logo echoes that contrast on this straight-cut denim wrap skirt, which was originally sold with the pin as its fastening.
note: The show report establishes Ford’s punk reference. The comparable wrap skirt has the original pin; the photographed skirt is missing its pin. No exact runway claim.

name: Beige Taormina Print Top
history: Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana drew on Sicilian imagery for Spring/Summer 2013. They put the same Taormina print on a sleeveless dress shown on the runway.

sources.title: Contemporary coverage and photograph of the sleeveless Taormina runway dress

note: The sleeveless dress was on the runway. The short-sleeve top shares its print and is not identified as a runway piece.

name: Black Asymmetric Pleated Skirt
history: Yohji Yamamoto used folds and uneven cuts to shape black skirts as early as Spring/Summer 1993. In his notes for that collection, he described working with folded fabric and curving cuts. On this skirt, layered pleated panels bring the fabric down to an uneven hem.

sources.title: Powerhouse Museum and Yamamoto’s collection notes

note: Yamamoto’s own notes document the earlier fold-and-cut method. The date of this skirt is unconfirmed.

name: Black Gothic Cathedral Mesh Top
history: For Fall/Winter 1998, Jean Paul Gaultier printed cathedral architecture and stained-glass motifs onto stretch mesh. A hooded top from the same season uses the same imagery. On this crewneck, the print runs across the body and down the sleeves.
note: The comparison is a hooded version of the cathedral print, not this crewneck on the runway.

name: Black Colourblock Portrait Mesh Top
history: Jean Paul Gaultier broke a portrait into concentric bands for Fall/Winter 2001. A snap-front mesh top from the season carried the print in colour. On this top, the portrait appears in black and grey across the back.
note: The snap-front top is a comparison for the portrait treatment. It is not the item being sold.

name: Peach Ruched Flared Trousers
history: Alexander Calder’s mobiles inspired the suspended shapes in Jean Paul Gaultier’s Spring/Summer 2003 collection. One runway look paired a top hung with geometric pieces with gathered pink trousers. This peach pair uses similar gathering at the knees above flared hems.
note: The show source establishes the Calder reference and a related gathered-leg design. The peach pair is not asserted to be the runway garment.

name: Olive Crinkled Cargo Shorts
history: Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana carried the crumpled finish of their previous womenswear collection into their Spring/Summer 2008 menswear show, where they used it on combat-inspired pieces. Look 24 paired this cargo-short design with a crinkled jacket.
note: Look 24 is cited as the cargo-short design match. The listing documents the sale example.

name: Black Fur-Trimmed Midi Skirt
history: Tom Ford worked fur into black knitwear for Gucci’s Fall/Winter 2002 collection. Liisa Winkler wore this skirt design under a satin coat in look 22, with its vertical fur strips and looped hem visible beneath it.
note: Look 22 is cited as the skirt design match. This does not establish runway provenance of the sale garment.

name: Navy Hooded Cardigan
history: Maison Martin Margiela took inspiration from the gesture of pulling a coat collar over the head to shelter from rain. On this cardigan, the extended collar drapes across the shoulders and becomes a hood when pulled up.

sources.title: R10 Margiela house notes, printed p. 280

note: Read the house’s original description of the rain-sheltering gesture on printed p. 280 of the thesis, alongside the item’s documented collar construction.

name: White Cotton Utility Jacket
history: Tom Ford shaped Gucci’s Fall/Winter 2003 outerwear around a cinched waist, opening the show with a white coat fastened by a broad corset belt. Curved topstitched seams bring that waist shaping into this shorter cotton jacket.

name: Black and Cream Floral T-Shirt
history: Roberto Cavalli drew on Chinese dress and ornament for Spring/Summer 2003, reworking the cheongsam as a fitted satin minidress. Eva Herzigová wore a silk dress with a version of this T-shirt’s floral print at the Milan show.

sources.title: Close-ups of the related silk cheongsam dress
Cavalli’s Elle interview excerpt, printed p. 118

item.title: Exact boutique item and garment photos

note: Herzigová wore a different garment with a version of the floral print. The interview documents the cheongsam reference, not the origin of the motif.

name: Red and Black Trompe-l’Œil Shirt
history: Jean Paul Gaultier experimented with prints that traced the body in the mid-1990s. A jacket from his 1996 ‘Cyberbaba’ collection mapped a nude figure in dots. On this JPG Jean’s shirt, curved stripes trace the torso across the front and back.
note: The museum piece documents the earlier body-mapping approach. It does not date this shirt to Spring/Summer 1996.

name: Black Layered Mesh Dress
history: Alexander McQueen used layers of sheer black fabric in his 2008 eveningwear. A strapless dress from Fall/Winter 2008 in LACMA’s collection layers strips of silk crepe through the skirt. On this cap-sleeve dress, a single layer of mesh extends below the opaque lining.

item.title: Exact boutique listing and label photos

note: The museum’s Fall/Winter piece is a different, strapless dress. This label supports 2008 only; no collection or runway match is established.

name: Ivory Tie-Waist Wrap Blazer
history: Around 2001, Tom Ford used ties in place of buttons on Gucci tailoring. A silk faille jacket from the period in LACMA’s collection fastens with narrow ties. This cropped blazer closes with a broad sash knotted at the waist.

sources.title: LACMA’s circa-2001 Gucci jacket and skirt with tied closure
Spring/Summer 2001 runway review, checked for context only

note: The museum ensemble shows a tied Gucci jacket from about 2001. It is not this ivory blazer; the item’s specific season is unconfirmed.

name: Black High-Rise Tailored Trousers
history: Maison Martin Margiela carried the high waist of Spring/Summer 2007 into the following winter collection. On the runway, look 29 paired a similar high-waisted cut with sharply squared shoulders.
note: The house notes support the high waist. Runway look 29 is a comparison for the cut, not a claim about this sale item.

name: Ivory Leather Lace-Through Boots
history: Dirk Bikkembergs drew on military, mountaineering and work boots for his early footwear. On this 1990s pair, the laces pass through the heel and wrap around the shaft, a fastening that recalls climbing boots.

name: Beige Crystal Fishnet Tank Top Set
history: Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana paired mesh and crystals on bras they showed as tops for Spring/Summer 2000, a combination they returned to on the fishnet tank. Jennifer Lopez wore a version in her 2002 video for ‘Jenny from the Block’, styled by Andrea Lieberman.

sources.title: Andrea Lieberman interview about styling the video
Surviving crystal mesh bra, design precedent

note: The video shows a version of the design. Spring 2000 supplies a material precedent; differing early-2000s dates for the set do not establish a specific season.

name: Blue Denim Maxi Skirt with Gold Sequins
history: Roberto Cavalli began embellishing jeans with leather patchwork in the 1970s. He returned to denim for Spring/Summer 2001, using gold-tone sequins to draw radiating lines across the long skirt shown on the runway.
note: Original runway image supports the skirt design; house history supplies the earlier denim precedent.

name: Knotted Wool-Blend Jacket
history: Rei Kawakubo launched Comme des Garçons Girl in Spring/Summer 2015 with rounded collars and separates drawn from school uniforms. This jacket keeps the rounded collar and places oversized fabric knots diagonally across the front.

sources.title: Exact style number and jacket photos
WWD Japan on the debut collection

note: The retailer style number helps identify this jacket. Line debut coverage supports the school-uniform reference, not that this later jacket was at the debut.

name: Brown Leather Aviator Jacket
history: Ann Demeulemeester worked with military dress and leather outerwear in the 2000s, pairing fitted biker jackets with jodhpurs on her Fall/Winter 2004 runway. This jacket uses an aviator cut, with shoulder tabs and an off-centre fastening.

name: Black Zip-Leg Leather Trousers
history: Tom Ford pared back the ornament for Gucci’s Fall/Winter 2001 collection and ran metal zips down the front of runway trousers in the place of tuxedo stripes. On this leather pair, the zips extend the full length of both legs.

sources.title: Contemporary Washington Post show report and Ford interview

name: Black Tie-Front Medallion Cardigan
history: Jean Paul Gaultier reproduced Pierre-Auguste Cot’s 1880 painting ‘The Storm’ in the medallion on the back of this Maille Femme cardigan. He showed the same image facing forward on an openwork knit in his Fall/Winter 2007 collection, which drew on dress from the Scottish Highlands.

sources.title: Kerry Taylor, comparable Maille Femme cardigan identifying the painting
Contemporary runway review, Scottish Highland dress context

note: The Met identifies Cot’s source painting, and runway look 45 shows the motif facing forward on a knit. Gaultier’s specific reason for choosing the painting is unconfirmed.

name: Black Leather Biker Jacket
history: Helmut Lang reworked the motorcycle jacket for Spring/Summer 2004. One version used cotton and cut-outs to lighten the heavy protective original. This leather version keeps the angled zip and broad lapels, with lace-up sides that release long ties below the hem.
note: The FIT label documents a related cut-out cotton biker jacket. The sale item is a different leather version.

name: Black Reconstructed Trousers
history: Martin Margiela began Artisanal in 1989 with a vest assembled from found porcelain shards. For Fall/Winter 2002, the house used reconstruction in its tailoring, joining matte upper panels to lustrous fabric on the lower legs of these trousers.

name: Blue and Yellow Orbital Print Top and Skirt Set
history: Issey Miyake developed a method of pleating clothes after they were cut and sewn. On this set, the orbital print runs across the narrow pleats of both the top and skirt.

name: Grey Military Shearling Coat
history: Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana drew on Napoleonic dress for Fall/Winter 2006, opening the show with a tableau of hussars and Empire gowns. They cut military tailcoats in shearling, carrying the uniform reference into plush collars and rows of metal buttons like those on this coat.
note: The runway review supports the Napoleonic reference and shearling at collection level.

name: Black Flared Trousers with Denim Panels
history: Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana cut up and reassembled denim for Spring/Summer 2001, sending out distressed jeans held together with safety pins. Another runway look used a shaped denim yoke with black flared legs, the construction seen on this pair.
note: The seller’s comparison connects the shaped denim yoke and black flares to a runway design. It does not establish provenance of this individual pair.

name: Black Sculpted-Shoulder Vest
history: Nicolas Ghesquière studied Cristóbal Balenciaga’s archive for Fall/Winter 2006, revisiting the founder’s moulded tailoring. A belted version of this sculpted-shoulder shape appeared on the runway over narrow trousers.
note: Ghesquière’s archive study is the collection context. The runway example is a belted version of the shape.

name: Black Feathered Mesh Top
history: Rei Kawakubo reworked Victorian and Edwardian tailoring for ‘Dark Romance, Witch’, her Fall/Winter 2004 collection for Comme des Garçons. The top she showed at the Lido in Paris pairs a sheer bodice with one tailored sleeve and a feathered shoulder.

sources.title: Original runway photograph, look 17 at the Lido

note: Look 17 supplies the one-sleeve and feathered-shoulder design comparison; styling on the runway need not be included with the sale top.

name: Black Cut-Out Leather Jacket
history: Paco Rabanne used slit openings to break up fitted outerwear for Fall/Winter 2000. A white coat in the show opened at the shoulders. This leather jacket carries the cut-outs across the chest and behind the elbows as well.

item.title: Archived jacket listing with runway comparison

note: The related runway design is a white coat with slits. The sale jacket is black leather and is not the same piece.

name: Navy ‘Doll’s Wardrobe’ Cotton Trousers
history: Martin Margiela first enlarged clothes from dolls’ wardrobes to human scale for Fall/Winter 1994, keeping the original proportions and small construction details. The label inside these trousers identifies them as a reproduction of a doll’s garment.
note: The Met explains the Doll’s Wardrobe project. The label on these trousers identifies the doll-garment reproduction.

name: Black Fringed Mini Dress
history: Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana used long fringe to interrupt the outline of their Fall/Winter 1993 eveningwear. On one surviving ensemble it hangs from a lace shawl. On this runway design, the fringe falls in tiers from the dress itself.

item.title: Exact boutique listing and runway comparison

note: LACMA’s dress-and-shawl ensemble documents fringe in the collection; the boutique’s runway comparison is separate evidence for the tiered dress design.

name: Black Micro Luggage Tote
history: Phoebe Philo introduced the Luggage in 2010, adapting a Céline suitcase design from the 1970s. Daria Werbowy and Stella Tennant carried the Luggage in the house’s Spring/Summer 2011 campaign, photographed by Juergen Teller.
note: The evidence is about the Luggage family and the 2011 campaign. It does not claim the sale bag itself appeared in the campaign.

name: Charcoal Layered Suede Jacket
history: For Yves Saint Laurent’s Fall/Winter 2002 collection, Tom Ford developed the fuller upper-body proportions he had introduced at Gucci. On this jacket, overlapping suede panels build volume across the shoulders and chest.

name: Black Wool Jacket with Detachable Mink Collar
history: Tom Ford revisited a tied-waist coat from 1999 in his final Gucci show, adding a fur collar to the new version. This black wool jacket appeared in the same Fall/Winter 2004 show with its own raised fur collar and low waist tie.
note: Ford’s earlier tied coat and this 2004 design are distinct. Keep the 1999 and 2004 references separate.

name: Black Multi-Strap Corset Top
history: Jean Paul Gaultier traced his corset designs to a salmon-pink girdle he found in his grandmother Marie Garrabé’s wardrobe. The Spring/Summer 1989 runway showed a peach version of this strappy corset shape, with the lingerie construction worn in view.

sources.title: R37 Palais Galliera on Gaultier’s corsets

note: The Galliera entry is a source for Gaultier’s corsetry precedent. The peach runway version is a comparison, not a claim about this black item.

name: Brown Silk Chiffon Dress with Slip
history: Jean Paul Gaultier used corset construction to shape printed silk chiffon in Spring/Summer 2004. A dress from that collection combines a corseted back with an asymmetric cut. This dress uses lacing at the back and lets the chiffon fall to an uneven hem.
note: Artcurial documents a different corseted chiffon dress from Spring/Summer 2004. The listing shows a separate slip included with row 38.

name: Silver-Painted Artisanal Blazer
history: For Fall/Winter 1999, Maison Martin Margiela painted over vintage menswear for its Artisanal line. On this blazer, the silver coating has cracked across the surface, with the original dark cloth visible beneath the lapels.

sources.title: R39 Kerry Taylor Artisanal blazer comparison

name: Red Gathered-Shoulder Corset Top
history: Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana brought lingerie onto the Spring/Summer 1991 runway, showing sequinned bra tops and bustiers alongside chiffon tunics. This red top carries the shaped cups into a square-necked bodice with gathered shoulders and long sleeves.

sources.title: Contemporary Los Angeles Times runway coverage

name: Black Fur-Trimmed Wool Cardigan
history: Tom Ford worked strips of fur into the seams of black knitwear for Gucci’s Fall/Winter 2002 collection. On this cardigan, those strips run across the body and sleeves, with long ends hanging past the hem.

name: Grey Trompe-l’Œil Cardigan
history: Martin Margiela had vintage garments photographed for Spring/Summer 1996, then transferred the images onto flat fabric. This cardigan reproduces a Shetland coat, with its lapels, buttons and back waist detail printed onto the jersey.

name: Multicolour Artisanal Patchwork Dress
history: For Spring/Summer 2005, the Margiela atelier cut up older dresses and reassembled them for its Artisanal line. On this dress, contrasting prints and sheer fabrics meet in panels that fall to different lengths.

name: Black Nylon Chocolate Bar Shoulder Bag
history: Chanel used square quilting on its early-2000s Chocolate Bar bags in materials including tweed and calfskin. This nylon version carries the same grid into a flap bag with a chain strap and interlocking CC turn-lock.

sources.title: R44 and R48 Chanel square-quilted comparison

name: Black ‘Flat’ Tailored Blazer
history: Martin Margiela took the paper patterns of his previous collection as the starting point for the flat garments of Spring/Summer 1998. The blazer design appeared on a hanger carried by a member of staff, showing its two-dimensional construction.

name: Black ‘Penelope Jaws’ Hoodie
history: Raf Simons drew on Ashley Bickerton’s use of brand logos for ‘Consumed’, his Spring/Summer 2003 collection. Working with Peter De Potter, he used that approach to collage a portrait of Penelope Tree with the shark from Steven Spielberg’s ‘Jaws’.

sources.title: Ashley Bickerton’s logo work at MoMA
Penelope Tree portrait and graphic comparison

note: The graphic comparison supports Penelope Tree and Jaws; it does not establish why the two images were paired.

name: Beige Tim Hawkinson Pleated Dress
history: Issey Miyake invited artists to work with Pleats Please beginning in 1996. For the third collaboration in 1998, Tim Hawkinson contributed an image of the body, its lines compressed and expanded by the pleats across the front of this dress.
note: LACMA documents the Tim Hawkinson collaboration and design; the listing identifies the sale dress.

name: Corduroy Hobo Bag
history: Chanel used square-grid stitching on its early-2000s Chocolate Bar flap bags. This hobo applies a similar grid to ribbed corduroy and wraps it around a curved body.

sources.title: R44 and R48 Chanel square-quilted comparison

name: Black Artisanal Chain-Trim Jacket
history: Maison Martin Margiela built its Artisanal line around the reworking of existing garments and materials. On this jacket, the seams remain visible, different fabrics meet at the cuffs, and metal chain edges the neckline and hangs in loops below the hem.
note: The house archive explains Line 0’s reconstruction method. The specific season is not confirmed in the copy.

name: Silver K&T Emerald Ring
history: Richard Stark fitted his early motorcycle leathers with sterling silver hardware. Chrome Hearts carried that metalwork into jewellery, using raised silver scrolls to frame the emerald on this K&T ring.

sources.title: R50 interview with the Chrome Hearts founders

name: Pale Peach Slip Dress

item.title: R38 listing, showing the accompanying slip

note: No history published. First establish whether this is a separate garment or the slip included with R38.

name: Off-White Western Denim Set
history: Slanted pocket flaps were a feature of Western denim shirts by the 1920s. Miu Miu gives that detail to the cropped denim jacket in this set, carrying the contrast topstitching onto the matching trousers.

name: Navy Funnel-Neck Zip Cardigan
history: By Fall/Winter 1999, Miu Miu was using full-length zips that closed into high collars on its knitwear. This navy cardigan carries the zip through a deep rib-knit funnel neck, with wide ribbing at the cuffs and hem.
note: The auction/archive comparison documents the high-collar zip treatment, not a match to this cardigan.

name: Black Coated Biker Trousers
history: Marithé and François Girbaud developed the Métamorphojean by placing seams around the body’s movement. These coated trousers use the same approach at the knees, where ribbed panels sit above horizontal zips.

sources.title: R54 Girbaud’s history of the Métamorphojean

name: Cream and Navy Striped Openwork Polo Top
history: Jean Paul Gaultier traced his interest in the sailor-striped top to childhood memories and Rainer Werner Fassbinder’s ‘Querelle’. This Maille Femme version works the stripes into an openwork knit with a crossover front.

sources.title: R55 Gaultier’s account of the sailor-striped top

name: Red and Cream Landscape Print Maxi Dress
history: Jean Paul Gaultier was using Japanese lettering in his dress prints by 1997. The ‘Fashion & Culture’ dress places bold brush lettering against blue and white. On this Gaultier Jean’s dress, vertical bands of lettering and circular crests cross a landscape of palm trees, blossoms and a red sun.
note: The 1997 archival dress is a Japanese-lettering comparison. It does not date the landscape-print dress to 1997.

name: Off-White Double-Layer Mesh Maxi Dress
history: Jean Paul Gaultier showed a similar two-layer dress in ‘Les Tatouages’ for Spring/Summer 1994, pairing a sheer outer layer with an opaque base. On this Gaultier Jean’s version, two ties fasten the mesh at the back, where the signature on the cotton dress remains visible.

sources.title: Kerry Taylor, comparable double-layer dress, circa 1994

note: Kerry Taylor dates its comparable dress circa 1994. The exact runway status of the photographed garment is not confirmed.

name: Stone Grey Lace-Up Nylon Skirt
history: Frida Giannini brought sports mesh, rubber lacing and motocross jackets to Gucci’s Spring/Summer 2010 runway. The same combination of mesh and crossed lacing appears here at the hips and waistband.

name: Black Lace-Up Shorts
history: Frida Giannini used crossed cords down the outside legs of fitted sportswear for Gucci’s Spring/Summer 2010 show. These cotton shorts place the same lacing at both hips.

name: Grey Houndstooth Biker Jacket with Detachable Fur Collar
history: Frida Giannini showed fitted motorcycle jackets in crocodile for Gucci’s Spring/Summer 2010 collection. This checked jacket uses the biker’s off-centre zip and fitted body, with a detachable fur collar.
note: 2010 runway biker jackets are a construction comparison. Do not use them to redetermine the 2009 title date.

name: Pink and Green Paisley Jacket and Skirt Set
history: Gimmo Etro introduced paisley into the house’s fabrics in 1981. Here the curling motif reappears on goatskin, spanning both the jacket and the skirt.

name: Black Corset-Shaped Leather Belt
history: Dean and Dan Caten drew on cowboy dress and ranch workwear for Spring/Summer 2006. The runway paired a broad leather belt with washed denim and a cowboy hat. This belt uses knotted leather cords and looped metal hardware at the front.
note: The runway comparison establishes the Western styling. It does not identify this exact belt on the runway.

name: Blue Denim Miniskirt with Geometric Panels
history: Dean and Dan Caten staged their Spring/Summer 2005 show as a house party, with washed denim among the clothes they styled for it. This skirt design appeared with a geometric fabric panel interrupting the denim at the hem.
note: The house show archive is the runway reference; the item listing is separate.

name: Olive Cotton Biker Jacket and Trousers Set
history: Dean and Dan Caten put protective pads at the elbows and knees in their Fall/Winter 2007 menswear collection. This set places ribbed stretch panels at those same points, where the jacket and trousers need to bend.
note: Fall/Winter 2007 protective panelling is a comparison, not a date assignment to the set.

name: Indigo Denim Harness Tote
history: Dean and Dan Caten used leather harnesses on outerwear in Fall/Winter 2003. On this denim tote, straps criss-cross both faces and meet at metal rings, with buckles at the sides.

name: Heather Grey Virgin Wool Coat with Fur Collar
history: Dean and Dan Caten set their Fall/Winter 2011 show in a snowbound version of the American West. Long coats and oversized fur were part of that wardrobe. This coat combines both in a straight wool body with a broad fur shawl collar.

name: Black Lace-Up Corset Pencil Skirt
history: Dean and Dan Caten staged their Fall/Winter 2010 show as a laboratory, mixing corsetry with biker clothes and anatomical details. The raised, lace-up waist on this skirt brings that season’s corset construction into a pencil silhouette.

name: Beige Frayed Linen Officer Jacket
history: Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana reworked Napoleonic uniforms for Fall/Winter 2006, using rows of metal buttons on officer-style coats. This linen jacket uses the same uniform details at the shoulders and cuffs, with frayed edges along the front.

name: Blue Denim-Print Pareo Skirt
history: John Galliano built the opening looks of Dior’s Spring/Summer 2000 runway around denim, with frayed skirts and lace-up boots. This pareo translates the denim into print, using pockets, seams and button flies to give the appearance of pieced jeans.

sources.title: R69 Dior denim at the Kyoto Costume Institute

note: The Kyoto Costume Institute documents Dior’s use of denim. The sale pareo is printed to resemble denim.

name: Tiger Stripe Capri and Pareo Set
history: Dolce & Gabbana introduced beachwear in 1989 and showed animal prints in its Spring/Summer 1996 ready-to-wear collection. This Mare set uses tiger stripes across two different weights of fabric, with fitted capris under a semi-sheer wrap.

name: Blue Pinstripe Officer Shirt
history: Nicolas Ghesquière used navy pinstripes in Balenciaga’s Fall/Winter 2007 menswear tailoring. This shirt pairs a similar pinstripe with contrasting shirt panels and shoulder tabs drawn from uniform dress.

name: Brown Fur and Nylon Crossbody Bag
history: Prada Sport paired goat fur with black nylon on bags for Fall/Winter 1999. On this crossbody, fur covers the front while the exterior zip pocket sits on the nylon back, just below the red Linea Rossa tab.

sources.title: Related Autumn/Winter 1999 Prada Sport fur-and-nylon bag
R72 Prada Group’s Linea Rossa history

note: Sizing remains on hold. The related fur-and-nylon bag is not a dimension or provenance source for the sale bag.

name: Navy Zebra Print One-Sleeve Dress
history: Peter Dundas used ruched animal prints and asymmetric cuts in Pucci’s Pre-Fall 2010 party dresses. This dress brings those treatments together with diagonal draping across the zebra print and a single long sleeve.
note: Pre-Fall 2010 is a related design reference only; the sale dress has no confirmed season.

name: Black and Cream Zebra Zip-Back Dress
history: By Pre-Fall 2010, Peter Dundas was using animal print and exposed zips across Pucci’s fitted party dresses. This wool-blend version sets the zebra pattern into a centre panel and runs a gold-tone zip down the back.
note: Pre-Fall 2010 provides a comparison for the material and hardware treatment, not a season assignment.

name: Pink Pleated-Shoulder Cotton Blouse
history: Frida Giannini set black buttons against bright pink on Gucci’s cropped jackets for Spring/Summer 2008. This cotton blouse uses the same contrast down a single placket, framed by pleats that fan out from the curved front yoke.
note: The runway reference is a cropped jacket in look 28, not this blouse. The comparison is the pink and black contrast. Leave the blouse’s season blank.

name: Brown Leather Dress with Beaver Fur Yoke
history: Frida Giannini moved towards longer day dresses for Gucci’s Fall/Winter 2010 collection and used fur in panels across the outerwear. The runway dress with this beaver fur yoke and metallic shoulder panels was styled with tall boots.
note: The runway design is cited for the fur yoke and shoulder panels, not provenance of the sale garment.

name: Red ‘P-Wing’ Varsity Jacket
history: Ralph Lauren introduced the winged-foot ‘P-Wing’ emblem in the 1992 Stadium capsule, which drew on vintage track and field. The emblem appears as a patch on the chest of this varsity jacket.

sources.title: R77 Ralph Lauren’s original Stadium capsule

note: The house’s original Stadium capsule explains the emblem. It does not date the sale varsity jacket to 1992.

name: Sand Asymmetric-Zip Cargo Jacket
history: Dsquared2 used off-centre zips and multiple utility pockets on its cargo jackets in the 2000s. A navy example from 2007 shows that combination. This sand cotton jacket places angled zips above flap pockets on a short, fitted body.

name: Black Ankle-Tie Cotton Trousers
history: Tom Ford used long ankle ties on trousers for Gucci’s Spring/Summer 2003 collection. A brown satin pair appears in the season’s campaign photographed by Mario Testino. On this black cotton pair, the ties cinch the straight legs at the ankle.

sources.title: Brown satin trousers and campaign reference

note: The campaign shows a brown satin example. The sale trousers are the black cotton version.

name: Black Convertible Jacket and Bucket Hat Set
history: Prada introduced Linea Rossa in 1997 with technical fabrics and fastenings drawn from sportswear. On this belted jacket, the sleeve zips let the wearer change it into a vest, and the matching hat carries the technical fabric into a stitched-brim shape.

sources.title: R80, R83, R84 and R88 Prada Group’s Linea Rossa history

name: White Zip-Front Cotton Cargo Skirt
history: Gaultier used exposed zips alongside workwear pockets on Femme jackets by Spring/Summer 1996. On this skirt, a full-length zip divides the front, with zipped and buttoned pockets set on either side.

name: White Zip-Front Cotton Cargo Blazer
history: A Spring/Summer 1996 Femme jacket paired silver zips and utility pockets with a cinched back. This blazer uses a similar pocket arrangement beneath notched lapels, with a tab that draws in the back waist.

name: Black Neoprene Waist Bag
history: Prada launched Linea Rossa in 1997 with a focus on technical sportswear. The MV563 waist bag has a small port for wired earphones, so a player could stay inside the pouch while the cable ran out.

sources.title: Prada Group’s original Linea Rossa press release
MV563 comparison listing (reference only, not sizing for this bag)
R80, R83, R84 and R88 Prada Group’s Linea Rossa history

note: Sizing remains on hold. The card supplies MV563; the separate model listing is a reference, not this bag’s measurements.

name: Black Linea Rossa Padded Parka
history: Prada introduced Linea Rossa as a technical sportswear line in 1997. This padded parka uses equipment details associated with snow sports, including an internal snow skirt and a hood that packs into the collar.

sources.title: R80, R83, R84 and R88 Prada Group’s Linea Rossa history

name: Yellow and Black Printed Down Jacket with Mink Collar
history: Miuccia Prada described her Fall/Winter 2004 prints as a meeting of eighteenth-century painting and video games. The runway used those digitally worked surfaces on fitted down jackets, including a yellow-and-black version of this print.
note: The show source supplies the painting/video-game reference. The colour and pattern comparison is separate from item provenance.

name: Black Fur-Trimmed Hooded Parka
history: Prada paired a fur-edged hood with leather trim on a perforated wool coat for Fall/Winter 1999. This padded parka places the leather at the waist, where a broad buckle belt draws in the shell.

sources.title: Gazette Drouot, Prada Fall/Winter 1999 coat, look 39

note: The Gazette Drouot coat is a different material and design. It is a comparison for fur edging and leather trim only.

name: Ivory Zip-Pocket Capris
history: Prada Sport used an exposed front zip and a zipped back pocket on cropped trousers for Spring/Summer 2000. This ivory cotton pair brings the hardware to the front, with long exposed zips beside smaller pockets.

sources.title: Spring/Summer 2000 Prada Sport capris and campaign reference

note: The Spring/Summer 2000 pair is a fastenings comparison, not a confirmed date for this ivory pair.

name: Silver Linea Rossa Hooded Parka
history: Prada developed Linea Rossa around technical fabrics and practical fastenings. This parka uses a metallic coated shell and incorporates a high chin guard and buckled cuffs into the hooded cut.

sources.title: R80, R83, R84 and R88 Prada Group’s Linea Rossa history

note: The Prada source documents Linea Rossa, not a precise season or an “Astro” attribution for this parka.

name: Orange Padded Nylon Gilet
history: Miuccia Prada put technical fabrics and buckle fastenings on the Miu Miu runway for Spring/Summer 1999. This nylon gilet uses a buckle to draw in the waist and sets contrasting trim around vertical zip pockets.

sources.title: R89 contemporary Miu Miu runway report

name: Black Cropped Zip Cardigan
history: By Fall/Winter 1999, Miu Miu was using full-length zips that closed into high collars on its knitwear. This cardigan uses that fastening on a cropped body, with a deep rib-knit hem and cuffs.

name: Navy Multi-Pocket Nylon Jacket
history: Miu Miu treated utility hardware as a visible detail in its early menswear. A pale jacket on the Spring/Summer 2000 runway had related chest-pocket hardware. This navy nylon version places D-ring tabs on boxed pockets.

sources.title: R91 Miu Miu menswear runway footage

name: Ivory Sheer Tie-Front Shirt
history: Jean Paul Gaultier Soleil was using sheer fabric with long waist ties by Spring/Summer 2002, when the treatment appeared on a printed wrap top. This shirt uses the ties to gather ivory mesh below a button front.

name: Copper Maxi Slip Skirt
history: Gaultier paired rib knit with crinkled silk chiffon on a skirt from the 2000s. This Femme skirt uses the same contrast in texture, with ribbed stretch panels above a flared, copper-coloured body.

sources.title: Into Archive, Gaultier rib-knit yoke skirt

name: Taupe Printed Mesh Twinset
history: By the mid-1990s, Gaultier’s Jean’s line was pairing cotton jersey with separate mesh layers. In Collection No. 0009, the line used the same printed mesh for both pieces of this twinset, a button-front shirt and a racerback tank.

sources.title: Kerry Taylor Auctions, circa-1994 Jean’s dress with mesh overlay

note: The circa-1994 dress documents layering within the line; it does not date this twinset or establish a common print.

name: Blue Ganesha Print Mesh Top
history: Jean Paul Gaultier Soleil was printing Indian imagery onto sheer mesh in the mid-1990s, including a top with figures from Indian cinema. This cotton mesh top places the elephant-headed Hindu deity Ganesha at the centre, framed by gingham.

name: Brown Pinstripe Zip-Front Cargo Blazer
history: Gaultier was combining tailored waists with utility pockets and exposed zips in his Femme line by Spring/Summer 1996. This cut also appears in white cotton. In brown pinstripe, the stacked cargo pockets interrupt the lines of a suiting fabric.

name: Black Fur-Trimmed Short-Sleeve Parka
history: Gucci made this short-sleeve parka as an outer layer in 2010. An archived example pairs the same fur-trimmed shell with a separate padded bomber, whose sleeves extend below the parka’s short sleeves. This listing is for the parka only.

sources.title: Boutique LUC.S, matching parka with the separate padded bomber

note: The archived ensemble documents the separate bomber. Only the outer parka is listed for sale.

name: Lime Green FF Terry Maxi Skirt
history: Karl Lagerfeld created Fendi’s double-F mark in 1965 for ‘Fun Fur’. The interlocking initials repeat tonally across the cotton-blend terry of this skirt.

name: Orange Buckled-Collar Biker Jacket
history: Dean and Dan Caten styled leather biker jackets for a music-festival setting at their Spring/Summer 2012 show. This jacket uses motorcycle details in stretch cotton, with a buckle at the throat and zips at the cuffs.

name: Pink Zebra Print Cotton Capris
history: D&G used pink zebra stripes on both flared jeans and cropped trousers. On this version, the print runs across a five-pocket cut that ends at the calf.

name: Black Linen Wrap Cargo Skirt
history: Dolce & Gabbana used cargo pockets on a wrap skirt for Spring/Summer 2003. The curved front panel sweeps below a zipped cargo pocket, while long ties at the waist adjust how far the two sides overlap.

sources.title: Elevated Archives, matching Spring/Summer 2003 wrap cargo skirt

note: The archived wrap cargo skirt supports the design and season attribution; the Option listing documents the sale example.

name: Taupe Linen Bomber Jacket
history: Dolce & Gabbana was making rib-trimmed bombers in linen blends by the 1990s. A related jacket has a stand collar and front flap pockets. This linen version places both pockets at the chest and adds a fastening tab at the collar.

name: Black Cable-Knit Cardigan with Faux-Fur Trim
history: Blumarine made fur-trimmed knits a house signature. When Nicola Brognano revisited its early-2000s designs for Fall/Winter 2021, he paired cable knit with faux-fur collars, a combination also used on this cardigan.

sources.title: R103 Brognano on the Blumarine revival

note: The 2021 runway is evidence of a revival, not the date of the sale cardigan.

name: Black Zip-Detail Stretch Top
history: Marithé and François Girbaud used the S.P.Q.R.CITY line to explore how performance fabrics could change everyday clothing. This Le Jean top applies a similar approach, combining stretch nylon with zip compartments and adjustable cords.
note: S.P.Q.R.CITY is a reference for performance fabrics. The sale top is from Le Jean; do not change the line attribution.

name: Brown Padded Gilet with Detachable Fur Collar
history: Prada paired fur trim with padded outerwear in Fall/Winter 2004, including a down jacket trimmed with mink. This sleeveless gilet uses dyed Kolinsky fur over a rib-knit collar, which can be worn on its own when the fur is removed.

sources.title: Into Archive, Prada Fall/Winter 2004 mink-trimmed puffer

item.title: Brown gilet listing and label photos

note: Fall/Winter 2004 is an outerwear comparison, not an exact season for this gilet. The gilet’s label documents its collar fibre.

name: Dark Olive Belted Leather Field Jacket
history: Trussardi began as a leather glove maker in 1911 and later applied its leatherworking to ready-to-wear under Nicola Trussardi. This jacket uses leather for a field-jacket cut, with a buckle belt and oversized flap pockets.

name: Indigo Linen Denim Trousers
history: Thierry Hermès opened a harness-making workshop in Paris in 1837. The straps and buckles printed inside the waistband and at the turned-up cuffs echo the horse tack made by the house.
note: The house documents its harness-making origin. The prints are a design echo, not a confirmed motif commission or collection date.
